paper_title: First Searches for Axions and Axion-Like Particles with the LUX Experiment
coupling_convention: canonical g_Ae (axion-electron coupling), dimensionless, as plotted on y-axis
notes: LUX 2013 data (95 live-days x 118 kg) axio-electric search. Two results: (1) galactic ALP dark matter: gAe < 4.2e-13 (90% C.L.) flat across masses 1-16 keV/c^2, assuming ALPs constitute all galactic dark matter (standard local density ~0.3 GeV/cm^3, not explicitly stated) — encoded above as the primary DM limit; (2) solar axions: gAe < 3.5e-12 (90% C.L.) for effectively massless axions (valid m_a < ~1 keV), corresponding to DFSZ mass limit 0.12 eV and KSVZ 36.6 eV — this solar bound is NOT a DM limit and is not included in data_points. Curve has a local bump near 4.2 keV, a dip near 5.5-6 keV, and rises to a peak ~4.5e-13 near 14 keV before dropping at the endpoint ~16 keV.
